title: Light, Truth and Honest Confession
overview: The letter opens by insisting Jesus was a real person the writers saw and touched, then says that being close to God means living in the light and being honest about our wrongs.

parts.label: Seen, heard and touched (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The writer never gives his name, though he is traditionally the apostle John. He says Jesus, called the eternal "Word of life" who was with God the Father from the beginning, became someone they could hear, see and even touch with their hands.

parts.label: Why they are writing (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: They pass on what they witnessed so readers can share their fellowship, a close bond with each other and with God the Father and his Son Jesus. Ancient copies differ on whether the writer says this makes "our" joy or "your" joy complete.

parts.label: God is light (vv. 5-7)
parts.note: Light stands for God's goodness, truth and purity, with no trace of evil in him. Claiming closeness to God while living in darkness is called a lie, while living in the light brings real community and cleansing through Jesus' death, which is what "blood" refers to here.

parts.label: Honest about failure (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: Anyone who says they have no sin is fooling themselves, and denying it even treats God's own word as false. Those who openly admit their wrongs find a God who is reliable and fair, who forgives them and makes them clean.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether being cleansed "from all sin" describes a lifelong process in which believers always keep struggling, or whether it allows for a deep freedom from deliberate sin in this life.
think: When has admitting a mistake out loud changed a relationship for you, for better or for worse?
